provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: B2b family batch, quote archetype override. Buyers are local businesses and fleet managers. No vinyl or film brands are named, and sign permit copy describes the shop's service only. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Vector file formats the sign shop accepts, what happens with a low-resolution logo, colour matching, how digital proofs are sent and signed off, and redraw fees
pageStructurePlus.why: Most sign jobs stall on artwork. A buyer who knows what file to send and how the proof works orders the same week.

pageStructurePlus.contains: One design across every truck and van, vehicle templates by make and model, a roll-out schedule that keeps vehicles working, and reorders when a vehicle is replaced
pageStructurePlus.why: Fleet managers buy vehicle graphics as a programme, not a wrap. Showing the programme turns one van into the whole fleet.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How the shop prepares drawings for monument, pylon and channel letter signs, works with landlord sign criteria, and coordinates the permit filing
pageStructurePlus.why: Permanent signs need landlord and city sign-off. Owners pick the sign company that takes that paperwork off their desk.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Cast versus calendared vinyl, full wraps versus partials and cut lettering, aluminum composite, acrylic, coroplast and banners, with indoor and outdoor use for each
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers compare quotes without knowing why one wrap or panel costs more. A plain materials guide explains the price before the call.

pageStructurePlus.section: Grand opening and event signage rush
pageStructurePlus.contains: Banners, window graphics, A-frames, trade show displays and temporary signs, with rush turnaround options and the cut-off for next-day pickup
pageStructurePlus.why: Openings and events have fixed dates. Customers with a deadline choose the sign shop that states its rush policy.

openers.line: You make signs so other businesses get found, and your own Maps listing has no website. A plumber who wants his van lettered can't see a single wrap you've done.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What your sign shop could look like behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your wraps and storefront signs look great on Instagram, but a fleet manager can't search it by vehicle type or tell what a partial wrap would run.
openers.hook: Check whether the listing or bio link goes only to Instagram or Facebook. Note the best vehicle graphics post.
openers.linkLine: Your sign and wrap work, sorted by job type: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still has a template banner and a photo gallery that won't load. For a sign shop, the website is the first sample of your design work buyers see.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale or broken thing. Note it plainly.
openers.linkLine: Same sign shop, with a site that shows the craft: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your sign site's gallery thumbnails stack into one long blur. Business owners pick a sign shop from their phone between customers.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your sign gallery, working on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to send your sign shop a logo file and the vehicle make before calling. A quote request that takes the artwork and the measurements would cut half the back-and-forth.
openers.hook: Check their site and listing for a quote form with file upload. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A sign quote request that takes the logo file: {demo-link}

openers.line: That box truck wrap you posted last month is already buried under newer vehicle graphics. A fleet buyer would want it on a page sorted by vans, trucks and trailers.
openers.hook: Find one wrap or fleet post that has scrolled down. Name the vehicle type if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your vehicle wraps in a gallery that stays put: {demo-link}

openers.line: A review praising your sign shop for turning a grand opening banner around overnight is exactly what a nervous new business owner wants to read before ordering.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about speed or a specific sign. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your turnaround reviews next to the sign quote form: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every new storefront in {City} needs window graphics, an opening banner and lettered vans in the same month. The sign shop they find first gets the whole package.
openers.hook: Look for new business permits or openings nearby. Use when a strip mall or new development is leasing up.
openers.linkLine: A grand opening sign package page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Owners plan their signage at night after closing their own shop. If your sign shop only takes requests by phone during the day, that order waits or goes elsewhere.
openers.hook: Note posted hours on the listing and whether anything takes a quote request after close.
openers.linkLine: A sign shop page that takes the order after hours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a wrap installer. Good installers check a graphics shop's work online before they apply, the same way your customers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a job listing. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A sign shop site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your crew installs channel letters and building signs well outside town, but nothing says how far you'll travel. A business in the next county assumes you won't come.
openers.hook: Look for install posts in other towns. Name the furthest one.

openers.line: Fleet wraps cost real money, and buyers ask about deposits, fleet pricing and paying per vehicle before they commit. A sign page that explains it removes the hesitation.
openers.hook: Only if they do fleet or full wraps. Check posts for multiple matching vehicles first.

openers.line: Business owners dread the permit and landlord approval for a monument or channel letter sign. A page that says your sign shop handles the drawings and filing answers their biggest worry.
openers.hook: Look for permanent sign installs in their posts. Never claim permits or licences you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Sign permits and landlord approval, explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like a lot of your sign work comes through printers, designers and other shops. When that partner closes or changes hands, the jobs stop unless buyers can find you directly.
openers.hook: Look for posts thanking a design agency or printer, or mentions of trade work. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a direct sign buyer would find you: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is sharp sign work. A job like that belongs on a page a business owner can forward to their partner before they order.
openers.hook: Pick their newest sign or wrap post and name it: the business type, sign or vehicle, and material.
openers.linkLine: That job on a sign shop project page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is sharp sign work.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the social pages, but nowhere a business owner could send a logo file or see your wraps sorted by vehicle. I put together a sample sign shop page with a quote request that takes artwork, a fleet graphics section and a materials guide, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last note got lost in the print queue. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a sign quote request with logo upload, a vehicle wrap gallery sorted by vans, trucks and trailers, and a grand opening package. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for sign shops and wrap studios here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No problem, you're busy weeding vinyl. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a quote form that takes the logo file, a wrap gallery by vehicle type and a materials guide, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a sign shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, about one partial van wrap."
"You know design better than most of my clients, so I'd value ten minutes of your eye on it this week."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: I design for a living. I can build my own site.
objections.handler: "You can, and it would look good. What I add is the quote request with file upload, the wrap gallery by vehicle and the pages that rank for sign searches. Your design, my plumbing, if you'd rather."

objections.objection: My work comes from walk-ins and referrals.
objections.handler: "Keep both. The site is for the fleet manager and the new storefront who search 'vehicle lettering near me' and never walk past your shop."
"Instagram is a great feed. A buyer looking for a box truck wrap can't filter it, and can't send you a logo file from it. The site pulls your posts into a gallery that sorts."

objections.objection: Online print shops already undercut me on banners.
objections.handler: "They do on banners. They don't measure vans, install channel letters or handle permits. The site leads with the sign and wrap work they can't do."
"Then let the site do the sorting. A quote form that asks for vehicle, artwork and deadline lets you take the fleet jobs and pass on the one-off magnets."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a quote form with artwork upload, a wrap gallery and a materials guide. That's about one partial wrap."

email.subject: Sign quote page for {Business Name}

{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} sign shop demo down on Friday.

Want me to leave it up? One word either way is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — new storefronts around {City} are lining up opening signage for the next quarter. Thought of you.

The sign and wrap site is still here whenever you want it, same price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one partial van wrap, never to a stack of banners.
The quote request with artwork upload is the core. Price the rest as additions to it.
Price the wrap gallery by vehicle category, not by photo count.
Let them art-direct; sign shop owners are designers and will pay more for a site they had a hand in.
Charge for the fleet graphics programme page separately; it sells to a different buyer than storefront signs.
Keep monthly add-ons under the price of a yard sign order so they never get questioned.

lineItems.item: Sign quote request with artwork upload
lineItems.description: Max with logo upload, vehicle year-make-model, side photos, sign dimensions, deadline and install address.
Max with filters for vans, trucks, trailers and boats, and full, partial or lettering on each job.
Max with a roll-out schedule layout, per-vehicle reorder form and fleet references the client supplies.
Max with photos of each substrate and vinyl type and indoor or outdoor use notes from the shop.
Max with bundled banner, window and door graphics and a rush order cut-off timer.
Max with the shop's drawing process, landlord criteria checklist and permit timeline in plain steps.

whatElseYouSell.name: Wrap and install photo sessions
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Finished wraps look best outside in good light. One session shooting the month's vehicles and sign installs fills the graphics gallery properly."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, then whenever a fleet job finishes.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for sign work
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each finished sign and wrap goes on your Google profile tagged by type, so 'vehicle lettering near me' finds fresh work."

whatElseYouSell.name: New-business welcome mailer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each month, new business registrations nearby get a postcard offering an opening sign package from your shop."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2. Uses public new-business filings in their county.

whatElseYouSell.name: Fleet manager outreach
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short note to local companies running unmarked vans and trucks, with a photo of a fleet you lettered and the fleet graphics page."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the fleet gallery has a few jobs.

whatElseYouSell.name: Wrap time-lapse reels
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Install day filmed from a corner of the bay becomes a short vehicle wrap reel for Instagram and the site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Any full wrap the customer approves for posting.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at pickup
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When a customer drives off in a freshly wrapped van, they get a short review request with a photo of their vehicle."

whatElseYouSell.name: Shop storefront and showroom refresh
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A sign shop's own window should be its best sample. I lay out the showroom wall and storefront graphics to match the new site."

withoutAI.route: Electricians who wire their illuminated signs
withoutAI.whoPays: The sign electrician, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who wires your channel letters and pylon signs? That electrician needs a commercial page as much as you did."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Sign electricians live on sign shop referrals and trust the shop's recommendation.

withoutAI.route: Fleet-owning trade businesses they wrap for
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The plumber whose vans you just wrapped has a great truck and no website. Your introduction gets me the meeting."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A freshly wrapped fleet with no site behind the phone number is the easiest pitch there is.

withoutAI.route: Commercial printers and promo product sellers
withoutAI.whoPays: The printer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The printer you send business cards and shirts to shares your customers and has an order page that doesn't work on a phone."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Printers and sign shops pass jobs back and forth daily.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your vinyl and substrate supplier sells to every sign shop in the region with a catalog nobody can search. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors have budgets and a ready list of sign shop customers.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The landlord whose sign criteria you work with every month has vacancies to fill. A leasing page with tenant sign rules helps both of you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords know the sign shop that installs for every new tenant.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The dealer whose lot banners and window stickers you print has an inventory page that's slow on a phone. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealers buy signage constantly and trust the shop that turns it fast.

withAI.route: Service call intake for the sign electrician
withAI.pitchLine: "Store owners report a dark channel letter or flickering cabinet sign, and the assistant books the electrician with sign type and photos."
withAI.whyItWorks: Electricians lose time on vague calls, and the sign shop sends them the customers.

withAI.route: Quote assistant for the commercial printer
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers describe the card, flyer or shirt order, and the printer gets a draft quote by quantity and stock that matches the sign shop's style."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built once around the sign client's buyers, sold through their trust.

withAI.route: Substrate and vinyl selector for the distributor
withAI.pitchLine: "Sign shops describe the job, indoor or outdoor, flat or curved, and the assistant suggests the substrate or film from the distributor's own catalog."
withAI.whyItWorks: It keeps sign shops ordering from one supplier.

withAI.route: Tenant sign criteria checker for landlords
withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants upload a sign drawing, and the assistant flags where it breaks the centre's sign criteria before the landlord reviews it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Landlords spend hours on sign approvals; the sign client knows the criteria first-hand.

withAI.route: Listing description writer for the dealership
withAI.pitchLine: "The dealer uploads a vehicle's details and photos, and the assistant drafts the listing and the window sticker text the sign shop prints."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dealers write hundreds of listings and the sign client already prints their stickers.

withAI.route: Brand kit builder for wrapped trade businesses
withAI.pitchLine: "A trade business with a new van wrap gets a matching brand kit: business cards, invoice header and social graphics drafted from the vehicle graphics."
withAI.whyItWorks: The wrap set the look; the kit sells naturally while the owner is excited about the van.

softwareAI.name: Proof approval links
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every sign proof goes out as a link with approve and request-change buttons, so no wrap goes to print on a verbal yes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their proof template and an email address customers recognise.

softwareAI.name: Sign and banner price calculator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers pick size, material and quantity for banners, yard signs and decals, and see your price before they call the sign shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price sheet for standard sign products.

softwareAI.name: Wrap mock-up from vehicle photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload the customer's van photo and logo, and it drafts a rough wrap layout on their own vehicle for the designer to refine."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past wrap designs and the designer's review of every draft. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job board from order to install
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every sign job on one screen: artwork, proof, print, laminate, weed, install, so nobody asks the owner where the banner is."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job steps and a screen in the shop.

softwareAI.name: Ready-for-pickup texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the banner or decals come off the laminator, the customer gets a text that the sign order is ready, with shop hours."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, with the job board. Needs customer numbers on each job.

softwareAI.name: Logo cleanup and vectorising helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload a blurry logo, and it drafts a clean vector trace for the sign designer to check before quoting a redraw."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the designer's review of every trace. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Vehicle template library
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every van and truck the shop has wrapped, with measurements, door handle and rivet notes saved by make and model for the next vehicle graphics quote."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the shop's past measurements and any templates they own.

softwareAI.name: Quote writer from walk-in notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The counter person types rough notes about a storefront sign, and a clean quote with material, size and install is ready to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past quotes and standard terms. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Fleet roll-out scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Fleet managers book each vehicle's wrap slot so no more than one truck is off the road at a time, with reminders the day before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, when the first fleet job lands. Needs bay capacity and install times by vehicle type.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and balance invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sign and wrap jobs get a deposit invoice at proof approval and a balance link at pickup or install."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their accounting system and deposit rules.

softwareAI.name: Sign permit packet builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Drop in the sign drawing, site plan and elevation, and it assembles the packet in the order the local sign permit office asks for."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the local permit checklists the shop already follows.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot for material and turnaround questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'how long does a wrap last' and 'can you do a banner by Friday' from the sign shop's own answers, then takes the artwork."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their materials guide and rush policy. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Material usage and job costing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which sign jobs made money once vinyl, laminate, substrate, ink and install hours are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs material use and hours per job for a few months.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for sign customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review of a sign or wrap gets a reply drafted in the owner's voice, mentioning the job, for approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Wrap care follow-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A week after a vehicle wrap, the customer gets washing tips; a year later, a check-in offering lettering updates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their care instructions and job dates.

softwareAI.name: Event signage order page
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Schools, churches and event planners reorder the same banners and yard signs each season from a saved sign order page."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs repeat event customers and their past orders.

softwareAI.name: Storefront mock-up from a street photo
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload a photo of the building front, and it drafts where the channel letters or window graphics would sit for the sign designer to refine."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the designer's review of every draft. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Social caption drafts for finished jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Snap the finished wrap or sign, and a caption naming the vehicle, material and business type is drafted for approval."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past captions they liked. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Installer applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Wrap installer and sign helper applicants answer the shop's questions on vinyl, heights and driving, and the owner only calls the fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they're hiring. Needs must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal for sign reorders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Franchise and multi-location customers reorder their approved signs and decals from a portal with their brand files saved."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once a multi-location customer reorders. Needs their approved artwork and prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the proof approval tool for sign shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Approvals by text message cause misprints in sign shops everywhere. My proof link tool fixes that for a small monthly fee."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first sign shop taught you the approval steps and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer locator for a vinyl distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Fleet buyers on your distributor site find a nearby wrap shop that buys your film. Your customers get jobs and keep ordering."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already compete for installer loyalty.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A member benefit every sign and graphics shop understands: a quote page with artwork upload and a gallery by job type."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons; one deal reaches many sign shop owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each sign franchise location needs local wrap galleries and a quote form routed to its own counter. One template, every location."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Signage ordering portal for a multi-location brand
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The brand's marketing or facilities team
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every location orders approved signs, window graphics and vehicle decals from one portal, printed by the sign shop."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brands lose control of signage across locations; the sign client becomes the default printer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Design agencies needing a print partner page
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies that design logos also need a page showing how brands go onto vans and storefronts. I build it with the sign shop behind it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell brand work and want production to look seamless.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I've built the wrap gallery and artwork upload for a sign shop in {City}. I'll only do it for one sign shop in your town too."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity by town sells, and the proof travels.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New chamber members get a starter sign and lettering package from a local sign shop, with a page that makes ordering easy."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chambers want tangible new-member benefits and local suppliers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your clients' vans need lettering at delivery and removal at resale. A graphics ordering page tied to your vehicle list keeps it in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Fleet managers handle graphics on every vehicle change, and the sign client does the work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Van wrap cost estimator with sponsor shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Trade owners pick their van and coverage, see a rough wrap price from the sponsoring shop's own rates, and send the request."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It never claims market data, only the sponsor's prices.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Takeover of half-built sign shop tools
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The sign shop with an unfinished project
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A sign price calculator or proof tool someone abandoned is a quick finish for me. I've shipped the same graphics workflow already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: They already budgeted for the tool; they need someone who knows the sign shop workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agents order yard signs, riders and open house signs from one page, printed and stocked by a local sign shop."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokerages reorder signs constantly and want brand consistency.

upsellLadder.offer: Sign shop site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The sign site and the care plan sit on one contract, so new wraps go into the gallery with a message to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a reprint caused by a misread approval.
upsellLadder.line: "That reprint is what proof links stop. Every sign gets a signed-off proof before it prints."

upsellLadder.offer: Google profile upkeep and review requests
upsellLadder.trigger: Several finished wraps are sitting in the camera roll unposted.
upsellLadder.line: "Those finished vehicle graphics should be on your profile this week, with a review request to each owner."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of quote requests show mostly banners, yard signs and decals.
upsellLadder.line: "Most of your requests are standard signs. Put prices on them and let customers order without the phone call."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first fleet job is finished and photographed.
upsellLadder.line: "Your first fleet is on the site. Now show it to every company running plain vans in {City}."

upsellLadder.trigger: A fleet customer asks to wrap several vehicles over a few weeks.
upsellLadder.line: "Let the fleet manager book each truck's wrap slot, and your bay is never empty or double-booked."

upsellLadder.trigger: A multi-location customer reorders the same signs for a new location.
upsellLadder.line: "Give that multi-location customer a portal and every new store's signage comes to your shop."
